Provinces affected (3) ITURI, NORD-KIVU & SUD-KIVU
Health Zones affected (26)
• Ituri (18/36) : Aru, Aungba, Bambu, Bunia, Damas, Gety, Kilo, Komanda, Lita, Logo, Mambasa, Mangala, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Nyankunde, Rimba, Rwampara, Tchomia.
• Nord-Kivu (7/34) : Beni, Butembo, Goma, Kalunguta, Katwa, Kyondo, Oicha
• Sud-Kivu (1/34) : Miti-Murhesa
Reporting date 09 June 2026
Publication date 10 June 2026

[PHOTO]

# 1. HIGHLIGHTS

• As of 09 June 2026, 37 new confirmed cases including 12 deaths, were reported in the health zones of Mongbwalu (13), Rwampara (11), Bunia (10), Tchomia (2) and Lita (1), in Ituri province.

• One (1) new health zone was affected in Ituri province: this is the Health Zone of Tchomia.

• Eight (8) confirmed patients with Ebola virus disease including 7 in the ZS (health zone) of Nyankunde and 1 in Mongbwalu (Ituri province) were declared cured.

• Launch of medical care activities in two (2) Ebola treatment centres (HGR [general referral hospital] Bunia and HGR Rwampara).

# 2. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Ituri province, located in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, shares a long and porous border with Uganda and South Sudan.
For more than two decades, it has been facing a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.
Its population is estimated at more than 8 million inhabitants, including more than one million internally displaced persons.
The health zone of Mongbwalu, considered as the starting point of the outbreak, is located in the territory of Djugu 70 km from Bunia.
This zone is characterized by the presence of armed groups, frequent population movements towards Uganda, and numerous artisanal mining sites attracting migrant workers.
In September 2018, Ituri province had already been affected by the 10th outbreak of MVE (Ebola virus disease) which was then raging in Nord-Kivu.
The current outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, was officially declared on 15 May 2026 by the Minister of Public Health.
The three affected provinces have a total population estimated at nearly 15 million inhabitants, with massive internal displacements and cross-border flows towards neighbouring countries.

[FIGURE: Figure 1. Chronology of events of the Ebola-Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak.]

The situation remains static in Sud-Kivu province, which had recorded its last confirmed case on 26 May 2026.

## 3.3 Temporal analysis:

An increasing number of confirmed cases is observed from one week to the next, reflecting continuous transmission of the disease in the community.
A sudden geographical expansion of the outbreak is to be feared if public health actions are not implemented quickly.

# 4. RESPONSE ACTIONS BY PILLAR

## 4.1 Coordination

National / Ituri :

• Organisation of ceremonies marking the recovery and discharge of patients in the health zones of Nyankunde and Mongbwalu.

• Conduct, on 08 June, of an assessment mission on preparedness in Kinshasa (hôpital du cinquantenaire) by the Chief of Staff to His Excellency the Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare with the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre.

• Continued support to the response pillars.

• Holding of the daily coordination meeting with PTFs and members of the SGI.

• Finalisation of the CONOPS.

## 4.3 Laboratory

• Ituri : 54 new samples collected and analysed (positivity 68,5% ; n=37)

• Nord-Kivu : 48 new samples collected of which 12 analysed, all returned negative for MVE as of 09 June 2026, 182 results remain pending due to insufficient reagents.

• Sud-Kivu : 2 samples received and analysed in the laboratory, all negative for MVE.

## 4.4 Infection Prevention and Control (PCI)

• Ituri : PCI (infection prevention and control) evaluation of 9 health care facilities including 5 in the Bunia ZS (score: 21 to 51,6%) and 4 in the Aru ZS (score: 16,6% to 33,3%); provision of handwashing kits to 154 TENASOSP and EXETAT examination centres; continuation of training for 50 care providers (20 supervisors and 30 focal points) from 16 ESS in the Bunia ZS on PCI; opening of the ring at CS Bora Uzima/Bunia ZS (households, churches and ESS identified); briefing of 51 care providers from 6 ESS in the Bunia ZS on waste management, hand hygiene, bio-cleaning, donning and doffing of PPE; briefing of 25 IT, 12 PPL (person released from treatment (discharged patient)) and 3 TS in the Aru ZS on waste management, bio-cleaning, donning and doffing of PPE; decontamination of HGR Rwampara where suspected and confirmed MVE cases were admitted; briefing of 6 local Red Cross workers from the Bambu ZS on EDS.

• Nord-Kivu : Scorecard evaluation of CS Katiri (69,4%) in the Kyondo ZS; the score obtained is 69,4%; holding of an introductory meeting of all partners involved in PCI for mapping and harmonisation of activities in the Katwa ZS; decontamination of 2 ESS around the latest confirmed cases in the Butembo ZS; exposure risk assessment of 8 care providers (6/8 high risk, all placed in quarantine) in the Butembo ZS; PCI evaluation of the MONUSCO Mubambiro site and accompanying the team for the implementation of PCI measures and guidelines on isolation of suspected cases; briefing of 6 providers from CS Kasisi on donning and doffing of PPE, risk assessment, cleaning and disinfection of premises.

## 4.6 Continuity of services.

• Conduct of the evaluation of HGR Kilo.

• Development of a human resources recovery plan (frontline providers).

## 4.7 CREC

• Nord-Kivu : 11 303 people (6 401 women and 4 902 men) reached through mass awareness-raising activities carried out in the community and 5 080 households visited reaching 24 671 people sensitized; 649 RECO (community health worker) mobilised, with coverage of 12 health areas out of 20 in the Karisimbi ZS; 340 people briefed on MVE prevention in the Nyiragongo and Karisimbi ZS; 212 pupils, 6 teachers and proctors sensitized in schools; 25 community alerts reported and 3 rumours collected then clarified; 18 local radios engaged with 3 radio formats produced and broadcast; a rapid CREC assessment in the demobilised combatants camp in Mubambiro in preparation and response to MVE with MONUSCO; visit to the Mukulya PoC/Beni ZS to conduct an assessment in order to strengthen CREC actions in support of traveller screening.

• Sud-Kivu : Organisation of 2 mass awareness sessions reaching 399 schoolchildren (168 Girls) from Camp Panzi (Ibanda ZS) and Bwindi (Bagira) on prevention measures and signs of MVE; support for the briefing of 45 community and religious relays in the Ibanda health zone with support from the Methodist church health coordination on MVE and community-based surveillance; posting of EBOLA communication materials at ports and strategic points in the city of Bukavu.

• Ituri : Reporting of an alert (suspected case who escaped from Mongbwalu showing hemorrhagic signs) by one of the traditional practitioners briefed by the CREC pillar.
He facilitated the transfer of the patient to the CTE (Ebola treatment centre) (AS [health area] Hoho, Rwampara ZS); development of a broadcasting schedule for testimonies of recovered patients from Nyankunde on local community radio; broadcasting of messages on preventive measures against MVE; organisation of 15 community dialogues with 125 people reached through topics on preventive measures against MVE, the dangers of self-medication and of confining suspected and/or confirmed cases; 139 people (52 men and 87 women) were reached during an educational talk; 9 mass awareness sessions organised, 3 108 people reached (1 528 M and 1 580 W) in 7 ZS with topics on preventive measures against MVE, the importance of SDB, the importance of community engagement, etc.; 4 advocacy meetings organised in the Rwampara ZS, 25 people took part (president of the IDP site, 10-house leader Katanyibwa, Kabanda military medical team).

• Support to other pillars : Surveillance: investigation and pre-listing of contacts (AS Mudzimaria/ Bunia ZS,).
PCI: Preparation of families to adhere to SDB in the event of community deaths (Bunia ZS, Bankoko and Bigo AS).
Result: SDB carried out.

Community feedback: (i) complaint related to care at the CTE; (ii) why SDB teams are excessively slow in their interventions; (iii) what steps to take to avoid mass contamination at the central market where people are too crowded; (iv) make PCI supplies (hydroalcoholic gel, handwashing kits) available to the population; (v) the population fears that graduating students who will be there for the Exetat exams may be a source of contamination.
Better to find them a centre for this in Bunia (Boga community radio).
Recommendations were formulated for adequate and targeted responses.

## 4.8 Logistics and Security

• Delivery of PCI supplies, medicines and equipment to the ZS of Lolwa, Gety, Lita, Rethy, Mongbwalu, Mandima, Jiba, Drodro, Komanda, Nyankunde, Fataki and Tchomia.

• 31 vehicles (2 operational ambulances.) ensure mobility of coordination, field teams in the various ZS.

## 4.9. Security

• The security situation in the city of Bunia (Bunia and Rwampara health zones) is relatively calm.
However, armed group activism in the territories of Djugu, Irumu and Mambasa continues to limit humanitarian access in several affected or at-risk health zones.

## 4.10. PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse)

• Briefing of 60 actors notably with WFP cooperating partners (38 participants: 14 women and 24 men) and providers from the Kalangane and Nuru AS in Sud-Kivu: 22 women).

• Sensitization on PEAHS of 20 (16W and 4M) church members from the St Véronique Cell in the Bunia ZS.

# 5. MAIN CHALLENGES


| No. | Challenges | Impact | Action required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (swabs) | Delay in confirmation; underestimation of cases | Intensive community engagement; involvement of religious leaders |
| 2 | Insufficient capacity in compliant CTEs despite the opening of Rwampara | Potential saturation of existing CTEs | Acceleration of construction of planned CTEs |
| 3 | Weak contact follow-up (overall rate 61,1%, target 95%) | Interruption of transmission chains compromised | Training, deployment and motivation of community relays |
| 4 | Lack of supply of Generic Essential Medicines (MEG) in targeted HGRs | Weakening of overall care | Advocacy for MEG provision |
| 5 | Insufficiency of PCI materials (PPE, DLM, chlorine) in Nord-Kivu | Nosocomial risk | Urgent supply |
| 6 | Low alert reporting in the 3 provinces | Delay in case detection | Strengthening of community surveillance |
| 7 | Insufficient financial resources for all pillars | Slowdown of operations | Resource mobilization (gap of 21,5 million USD) |
